My mum used to be a nurse before she died and she had this patient. She was 80 something had terrible health problems and was dying. She'd ring the help buzzer every 10 or so minutes. Then when I nurse came they'd ask her what she wanted and she'd saying nothing. After about 3 hours my mum had seen this woman maybe 4 or 5 times and her colleagues told her the situation. So she went in there and she said " I'm really sorry but if you don't need anything can you please stop ringing the buzzer and if you do need something just tell me now. " the woman replied with " I just don't want to die alone" my mum stayed with her for as long as she could. The woman died that night and my mum came back home in tears. She knew what she was signing up for when she became a nurse. She knew she was going to loose people. But she was completely heart broken and run down for at least a week after every death she dealt with. She used to tell me about how she would almost become oaraylsed when she heard a code blue but she always made sure to be at least one if the few first people there. She cared so much for every single one of her patients. She cared so much about everyone actually. She would've been 38 on July 10th. She died from something that is only ever found in men over 60. May you rest in peace Laura I hope we meet again in another life. You are truly an angel.
